title: Graphs
hook: Graphs are nodes plus edges that can go any direction — not just parent/child.

steps.caption: From A you can reach B and C — edges define the legal moves.

nodeCaptions.a: A node’s neighbors are whoever its edges point to.
nodeCaptions.b: Unlike a tree, B might also link back or sideways.

steps.caption: B connects to D. Cycles are allowed — you can return to a node you’ve seen.

nodeCaptions.d: Traversal algorithms mark visited nodes so cycles don’t loop forever.
nodeCaptions.c: Social nets, maps, dependencies — graphs show up everywhere.

takeaways: Graphs generalize trees: edges aren’t limited to a single parent.
Traversal needs a visited set when cycles exist.
Many real systems are graphs: networks, deps, recommendations.

quiz.question: What makes a graph different from a tree?
choices: Edges can form cycles and aren’t limited to parent/child
quiz.explanation: Trees are a restricted kind of graph. General graphs allow richer connectivity.
